name: Sveltia CMS
title: Mica vs. Sveltia CMS
summary: Sveltia CMS is a fast, Decap-compatible editor with first-class languages, many media providers and a preview pane. Mica keeps large files out of the Git history on GitHub too, supports submodules, and has an MCP server for AI agents.

chooseMica.text: You want AI agents to edit your content: Mica has an MCP server built in. Sveltia CMS has no MCP server.
Your editors should see the real page beside the form, and click a text to edit it. Mica needs no change to your templates.
You have many large photos or files on GitHub, which would bloat your Git repository. Mica keeps them out of the normal history, with Git LFS.
Your entries link to data that lives elsewhere: product data, place names, regions or codes. Mica uses thousands of items from a JSON or CSV file of your website, and never edits them.
You keep your content in a Git submodule, apart from the code of your website.
You expect thousands of entries and files. Sveltia names small to medium-sized projects as its target.
You want sign-in through your OpenID Connect provider.
An editor should publish several changes as one commit, with a summary.
You need a map to pick places, and the page should show the same view: Mica stores the zoom with the place.

chooseOther.text: Your content has several languages, and you want machine translation.
You want media in S3, Cloudinary or another provider, not in Git.
You want a two-pane live preview with scroll sync, from React templates of your own.
You want an address search on the map.
Your Git host is GitLab or Gitea, and you want an editor with no server to run.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo and Codeberg. No Bitbucket or Azure. Local mode uses the File System Access API of the browser (Chromium only).
Yes. It is a static app. GitHub OAuth needs a server. GitLab and Gitea use PKCE without a server. Personal access tokens also work.
No. It caches in the IndexedDB of the browser.
config.yml, TOML, JSON or JavaScript. It is compatible with Decap CMS.
A framework guide and community starters. Content Collections read the files.
GitHub OAuth, GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo PKCE, tokens. OIDC and SSO are not documented.
simple: each save commits. preview: changes go to a pull request. editorial_workflow: one pull request for each entry, with statuses. No batch publish documented.

A two-pane live preview with scroll sync, from custom React templates in a sandboxed iframe. Deploy previews of unpublished entries through CI. The roadmap lists an out-of-the-box live site preview as a non-goal.
On GitLab and on Gitea/Forgejo (large files stay outside the normal history). Not on GitHub.
Not supported. Local commits are refused in a submodule.
Stores a GeoJSON string. The center and the zoom only set the first view and are not stored. Address search with Nominatim.
Not documented. Relations point to collections or to list items in a file.
First-class, with machine translation through your own API key.
None yet. An add-on is planned. Review goes through the editorial workflow.
No MCP server. It has an Agent Skill, llms.txt and AI translation.
